answer.short:
$X(-2,3)$

Double the centre coordinates, then subtract the coordinates of Y.
answer.worked:
The midpoint of the diameter is the centre.
$$\begin{align*}
\frac{x_X+4}{2}&=1\\
x_X+4&=2\\
x_X&=-2\\
\frac{y_X+(-1)}{2}&=1\\
y_X-1&=2\\
y_X&=3
\end{align*}$$
$X(-2,3)$.

children.prompt: What fraction of the vertical distance between the end points is $P$ from $A$?

answer.worked:
$P$ is the same fraction of the vertical distance from $A$ as of the horizontal distance.
$$\begin{aligned}\text{Fraction}&=\frac{1}{1+2}\\&=\frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}$$

The coordinates of $P$ are one third of the distance from $A$ to $B$.
$$\begin{aligned}x_P&=-3+\frac{1}{3}\bigl(3-(-3)\bigr)\\&=-1\\y_P&=-1+\frac{1}{3}\bigl(2-(-1)\bigr)\\&=0\end{aligned}$$
$P(-1,0)$

flags.note:
[Pedagogy review · High priority · opening-review · pf-d14351f00b]
Finding: The midpoint topic has no opening review of signed addition and formula substitution, both used directly in its introductory examples.
Breakdown: Students must substitute signed values into corresponding positions and evaluate signed sums while learning the midpoint formula. Neither prerequisite is rehearsed before these examples.
Checked: All supplied teaching was checked. This is the first topic, and it contains no review. Both introductory examples require substitution and signed addition.
Assumes: These are prior skills, consistent with the course library. Calculator availability does not remove the substitution requirement.
Proposed repair (add-review): Before p3-formula, add: (a) Calculate -4+8. (b) Calculate 3+(-5). (c) Given F=(a+b)/2, substitute a=-6 and b=10 and evaluate F. (d) Given G=(c+d)/2, substitute c=2 and d=-7 and evaluate G. Answers: 4, -2, 2, -2.5.
Done when: A short opening review rehearses signed addition and substitution before the midpoint teaching.

[Pedagogy review · High priority · unsupported-transition · pf-8842902d42]
Finding: Unequal division requires a coordinate calculation that the preceding teaching does not supply.
Breakdown: Parts p7-q8-a and b identify the fraction of each displacement, but do not explain adding that fractional displacement to the starting coordinate. Students may instead multiply B's coordinates by the fraction.
Checked: The complete preceding teaching supplies midpoint averaging and inverse midpoint practice, but no unequal-division calculation. The diagram and fraction questions identify the displacement fraction without showing the coordinate offset.
Assumes: Ratio-to-fraction conversion and basic signed arithmetic are prior knowledge; unequal coordinate division is a new variant.
Also affects: p7-q9, p7-q10
Proposed repair (add-teaching): Between p7-q8-b and c, add: 'Start at A and add one third of the change from A to B in each coordinate. For x: x_P=-3+(1/3)[3-(-3)]=-1. Use the same method for y.' Leave students to calculate y and assemble P.
Done when: Students see start + fraction × signed coordinate change before completing the unequal-division tasks.
